ai.description: The Splendid Krait reaches 1.5 meters. It is black with large, white, squarish dorsal blotches and a yellow head. It features a distinct vertebral ridge and a rounded, non-flattened tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Bungarus magnimaculatus* is distinguished by its distinct, large, squarish white blotches along the dorsal midline, which are significantly broader than other kraits.
ai.habitat: The Splendid Krait inhabits tropical deciduous forests and scrublands in Myanmar and adjacent regions, typically found at low to moderate elevations.
ai.behavior: The Splendid Krait is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt other snakes, lizards, and small mammals across its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: The *Bungarus magnimaculatus* is oviparous, laying clutches of 8–12 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Splendid Krait (*Bungarus magnimaculatus*) is endemic to Myanmar and is not found in the Indian subcontinent.
